## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical expertise in multi-tenant security, using real-world tools (cosign, Rekor, Kyverno, KMS) to enforce image provenance at CI time. It emphasizes tenant isolation, key management, and concrete verification steps.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign-based image signing with per-tenant keys stored in a central KMS
- Rekor-backed provenance verification
- Kyverno policy enforcing signatures and digest pinning across repos
- CI gating via GitHub Actions, plus local verification workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions gate (high level)
name: Image Signatures Gate
on: pull_request
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install cosign
        run: curl -fsSL https://toolkit.cosign.is/cosign-linux-amd64 -o /usr/local/bin/cosign && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cosign
      - name: Fetch tenant key from KMS
        run: |
          echo "Fetching tenant key..." # placeholder
      - name: Verify images in manifests
        run: |
          cosign verify --key <tenant-key> image digest
```
```yaml
# Kyverno policy snippet (digest-signature & tag checks)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-cosign-signature
spec:
  rules:
  - name: image-signature
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment, Job, KnativeService]
    validate:
      message: "Image must be cosign-signed with tenant key"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: ?*
              - imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate tenant keys without downtime?
- How would you audit failures and respond to a signature mismatch in production?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce cross-tenant GPU isolation using Gatekeeper/OPA, Node labeling, and named GPU types in a realistic Nvidia/HashiCorp context.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes admission control
- OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate
- Node labeling and NodeAffinity
- Per-namespace allowlists and error messaging
- Testing with conftest and end-to-end scheduling

## Code Example
```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate sketch (simplified)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: gputypematch
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: GPUsTypeConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package gputypematch
      violation["msg"] = msg :-
        input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
        and some container in input.review.object.spec.containers
        and container.resources.requests["nvidia.com/gpu"] > 0
        and not input.review.object.spec.nodeSelector["gpuType"] in allowed_types
        and not input.review.object.metadata.namespace in namespace_allowlist
        msg := "GPU type not allowed in namespace"
```

- What are trade-offs of using nodeAffinity vs taints/tolerations for GPU types?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

### Follow-up
- Extend to handle missing tests per service gracefully
- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

## Why This Is Asked

name: Secrets Scan
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

          set -euo pipefail

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests end-to-end security design for multi-cloud Kubernetes workloads, focusing on identity, secret management, and policy enforcement with real-world tools.

## Key Concepts
- Zero-trust workload identity (SPIRE)
- Ephemeral credentials (Vault)
- Service mesh security (Istio, mTLS, AuthorizationPolicies)
- Policy-as-code (OPA/Rego)
- Egress controls to data lake and namespace isolation

## Sample Solution

### 1. SPIRE Workload Identity
```yaml
# spire-workload.yaml
apiVersion: spire.spiffe.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterSPIFFEID
metadata:
  name: data-platform-workload
spec:
  names:
    - data-service
    - analytics-service
    - etl-service
  namespaceSelector:
    matchLabels:
      environment: production
```

### 2. Vault Integration for Secrets
```yaml
# vault-secret-store.yaml
apiVersion: secrets.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: VaultSecret
metadata:
  name: data-lake-credentials
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  vaultAddress: https://vault.data-platform.svc.cluster.local:8200
  path: secret/data-lake
  provider: hcp
  refreshInterval: 1h
```

### 3. Istio AuthorizationPolicy
```yaml
# istio-authz.yaml
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: data-lake-access
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: data-lake-gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://data-platform/data-service"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET", "POST"]
        paths: ["/v1/tables/*"]
```

### 4. OPA Policy Example
```rego
#.rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.namespace == "restricted"
  not input.request.object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
  msg = "Pods must run as non-root"
}

allow[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  input.request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_].securityContext.privileged
  msg = "Privileged containers not allowed"
}
```

### 5. CI Enforcement Check
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Security Scan
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  opa-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run OPA policy check
        run: |
          opa eval --fail-defined-deny \
            --data policy.rego \
            --input manifests/
```

## Key Takeaways
- SPIRE provides cryptographically secure workload identity
- Vault enables dynamic secret rotation without application changes
- Istio mTLS ensures service-to-service encryption
- OPA/Rego enforces admission control and runtime policies

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of cross-environment image provenance and automated attestation in a multi-cloud setup.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-registry signing and verification

## Code Example
```bash
# Sign and verify (example for AWS KMS key)
cosign sign --key 'kms://aws/kms/cosign' ghcr.io/org/service:tag
cosign verify --key 'kms://aws/kms/cosign' ghcr.io/org/service:tag
cosign attest ghcr.io/org/service:tag --predicate attest.json --type intoto
```
